text: One payment, across a border, split three ways. Confirmed in under two seconds.
Exporter in India, buyer overseas. A SWIFT wire pays sixty to ninety days later. On Monad, one A U S D payment settles in seconds.

First, passkey onboarding. On the buyer card, tap sign up with passkey and approve with Touch I D. Privy creates an embedded wallet on Monad: no seed phrase, no extension. The card now reads passkey wallet, with its own address, and one tap funds its gas.
The rest runs on burner wallets. The exporter loads a shipment: forty-eight thousand seven hundred fifty dollars, offer thirty-nine thousand.
Now the A U S D balances, all zero. The lender mints a hundred thousand test A U S D, it lands in their wallet, and depositing it grows the pool balance by exactly that.
The buyer signs the invoice with an E I P seven-twelve message, which unlocks the advance.
Now, send and receive. The exporter accepts, the pool sends thirty-nine thousand A U S D, and it lands in the exporter's wallet. Confirmed in about one point three seconds.

Then the buyer sends forty-eight thousand seven hundred fifty across the border. The exporter's balance jumps, and one transaction has split it: just over forty thousand to the pool, a twenty-six dollar fee, and eight thousand seven hundred twenty-two to the exporter.

Why Monad? Four hundred millisecond blocks, fast finality: settlement in seconds. One dollar asset for everyone, so no F X step onchain. On testnet, A U S D is a six-decimal mock with the same interface.
Passkey in, A U S D balance, a payment settled in seconds. Hisab on Monad.
